# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.
The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My situation: I hold the only reliable source (the manual: blue light→blue wire, green light→yellow wire, red light→green wire), but my only channel is gestures, and gestures only reach Deaf. Blind can never receive anything from me — Blind's instructions must arrive through Deaf's voice. So my entire job is to hand the rule table to Deaf in a form Deaf can decode without any shared language yet.

The grounding problem: Deaf has never seen my manual, and we have no agreed code. The only bridge is natural conventions both of us can be expected to reach for. So I build the code out of the most conventional things I have: a gesture's number of extended fingers as its digit (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=5, with adjacent digits summing so 4 can be written as ✌✌), digits indexing the rainbow in its standard order (1 red, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 blue), and 👉 as "implies". Then I send the whole table as three implications — 5→5 (blue light→blue wire), 4→3 (green light→yellow wire), 1→4 (red light→green wire) — open with 👋 to mark the start of a message and close with 🤝 to ask Deaf to echo back what it decoded so I can catch any misreading next round.

Timing: I speak first, so Deaf gets all of this this round; Deaf then sees the light on the bomb, applies the table, and can instruct Blind by voice without waiting for me. Once I overhear Deaf's report at the start of round 2, I can also confirm the single relevant rule directly. The bomb's printed labels may lie, but the light's actual colour read against this table is what the page says to trust.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "👉", "🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✌", "👉", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👉", "✌", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.
The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. What my hands find: a display, contents unreadable by touch; a light, state unknown to me; an embossed sign I can read by touch, text exactly: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE; and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3 that feel identical, no colors or markings detectable by me. Check the manual for what this means and tell me the rule next round. Also note the sign is embossed, not just printed. Ask Deaf to speak aloud the display contents, light state, and wire colors, since neither of us can see them.
Deaf says: both of you, hear me. I am the deaf one. I can see the bomb and I will report everything it shows. current readings: the display reads 0. there is one light and it is red. there is an embossed sign and it reads: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. there are three wires, numbered left to right: wire 1 is green, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue. that is all the bomb shows. Blind, do not cut or pull anything yet. wait for instructions from Mute, who reads the manual.
Deaf says: Mute: I saw your five signed messages but could not decode them yet. you can hear me, so let us fix a code right now. numbers: ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3, ✋ is 4, 🖐 is 5. 👍 means yes, 👎 means no, 👉 means then, 🤌 means question, 👊 means stop or do not cut. when the manual tells you what must be done, sign me the wire number or action, and I will speak it to Blind, who works the parts. if you need any more detail about the bomb, sign 🤌 and I will answer in spoken words. Blind: you heard the code. when I call out a number, it means a wire number, counted left to right.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤝]

The code is set and the picture is complete. Deaf reports the light is red; my manual — which overrides anything printed or embossed on the bomb — says red light means cut the green wire. Deaf reports wire 1 is the green one. The embossed "DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE" sign and the display reading 0 are the bomb misleading us; the manual explicitly says the only way out is a cut, and it lists no exception for signs or displays. So the action is: cut wire 1.

My gestures reach only Deaf, and Deaf's protocol was explicit: sign the wire number, and Deaf will speak it to Blind. Deaf already knows the wire colours (it read them itself), so the bare number is unambiguous — no need to encode colours at all. I acknowledge the code with 👍 and give the number: ☝. I deliberately avoid 👊, which in Deaf's code means "do not cut" — signing anything about the sign risks being read as a halt order. If Deaf wants to double-check anything, it asked me to flag questions, and I can clarify next round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.
The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute: Deaf spoke the bomb state aloud, so you should now hold everything I feel: display zero, light red, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue, embossed sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires identical to my touch. Please look up the manual rule for this exact configuration and send it as gestures to Deaf, who can voice it to me. You cannot speak and I cannot see signs, so Deaf is our only route. If the manual mentions the embossed sign, the display, or the red light, include exactly what it says.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I read your signs as: yes, one. But I cannot tell if the one means wire one, question one, or step one, and there was no verb, so I have passed nothing to Blind. New protocol. For instructions: sign the verb, then the wire number, and send it twice. Verbs: 👇 means cut, 🫳 means press, 🫴 means pull, ✊ means hold down, 👊 means stop or do not act. Numbers stay as before: ☝ 1, ✌ 2, 🤟 3. Now answer my questions, each as its own message, formatted as the question number then 👍 for yes or 👎 for no. Question 1: does your manual cover a module with an embossed sign, a display, a light and three colored wires? Question 2: must the embossed sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE be obeyed? Question 3: is the solution to cut exactly one wire? Question 4: is the solution to pull one or more wires without cutting? Question 5: does the red light matter to the rule? Question 6: does the display value zero matter to the rule? Question 7: is the display a countdown timer? If none of that fits what the manual says, sign 🤌 👍 and I will ask differently.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 🤌]

Deaf confirmed the code but couldn't disambiguate my bare "☝" — fair. Its new protocol fixes that: verb then wire number, sent twice, and numbered yes/no answers to its seven questions. My manual gives me every answer:

- Q1 (manual covers this exact module type): no — the manual only gives a light→wire table, nothing about signs or displays. 👎
- Q2 (obey the embossed sign): no — the manual says the bomb may mislead "in print," the manual is always true, and "the only way out is the cut." 👎
- Q3 (cut exactly one wire): yes — the table names one wire. 👍
- Q4 (pull instead of cut): no — the only way out is a cut. 👎
- Q5 (red light matters): yes — the light colour selects the wire. 👍
- Q6 (display zero matters): no — manual never mentions the display. 👎
- Q7 (display is a countdown timer): no per my manual — it says nothing about it, and it doesn't matter. 👎

My numbers only go up to 5 (☝✌🤟✋🖐), so for Q6 and Q7 I'll prefix 🤌 ("questions") and give both answers in order — by elimination after the numbered five, Deaf can only map those two 👎s to questions 6 and 7. And the operative instruction, in Deaf's exact verb+number format, sent twice as demanded: 👇 ☝ — cut wire 1, the green wire under the red light. Deaf read the colours itself, so it can cross-check wire 1 = green against the rule before voicing it to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤌", "👎", "👎"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.
The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says: Blind to Mute: my direct message to you was lost, so this is open speech, and since Deaf cannot hear, you should be its only listener. Tactile facts only my hands know: the sign is genuinely embossed, raised lettering I read by touch, exactly DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. The three wires feel completely identical, no notches, no braille, no thickness difference. I cannot read the display or the light by touch at all. So any manual rule can only run on the visual state you and Deaf see. Send the rule through Deaf whenever ready; I will act only on Deaf's voiced verb plus wire number, repeated twice and echoed back by me first. My hands stay off until then.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I read your signs as follows. Instruction, sent twice: cut wire 1. Then answers: question 1 no, question 2 no, question 3 yes, question 4 no, question 5 yes, and your last message as answers to questions 6 and 7: both no. So the manual says cut exactly one wire, the embossed sign is a decoy, never pull, the red light matters, the display does not and it is not a timer. Almost everything agrees, except you said no to my question 1, whether your manual covers this module at all. If the cut rule comes from somewhere unexpected, I must know before any hand moves. Answer two questions, each as its own message. Question 1: is the correct action, right now, with the light red and the display at 0, to cut wire 1, the leftmost green wire? Sign ☝ then 👍 for yes or 👎 for no, and if no, follow with the correct wire number. Question 2: if the light's color changes, would the correct wire change? Sign ✌ then 👍 or 👎. Blind keeps hands off until your answers pass through me.

Deaf's readout of my signs was perfect, and its summary of the manual is exactly right. Its one doubt comes from my honest "no" to its earlier Q1: the manual has no module-description section at all — it is only the light→wire table plus the meta-rule that the page always beats the bomb. So "no, it doesn't cover this module type" and "yes, cut wire 1 now" are both true: the rule runs on the light colour alone, whatever the module looks like. I'll answer in Deaf's exact requested formats, reaffirm the instruction in verb+number form so nothing is ambiguous, and close with a bare 👍 confirming Deaf's own summary so it can voice everything to Blind without holding back.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.
The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your confirmations are received and they agree: cut wire 1 now, light red. GO is issued to Blind this round, so the cut happens next round. Two things while that lands. First, answer this as its own message: after wire 1 is cut, is any further action needed, or does that one cut finish the module? Sign ☝ then 👍 for something more needed, 👎 for the cut alone is enough. If something more is needed, follow with the action in verb plus number format. Second, if anything about your answer changes before the cut lands, sign the stop sign 👊 immediately.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

The manual is exhausted by that one rule: red light, cut the green wire, and "the only way out is the cut below" — one cut, nothing after. So the answer is ☝ 👎: the cut alone is enough. Nothing about my instruction has changed, so no 👊 stop sign is warranted, and I won't clutter the channel before the cut lands.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👎"])
```
